items.headline: Government to develop the Gillman Barracks and Maju Forest sites, though designs are not finalised
items.summary: Minister of State for National Development Alvin Tan told Parliament on 4 August that the two sites are zoned residential and will be built on, while fielding questions from at least 13 MPs. Two petitions against clearing the forest patches have drawn more than 46,000 signatures, with public feedback on the environmental studies closing 6 August.

items.headline: GovTech's retrenchment of 93 officers draws scrutiny in Parliament
items.summary: MPs pressed the digital ministry on 4 August over GovTech's 15 July layoff of 93 officers, part of a shift to a product-ownership operating model expected to affect about 300 staff over two years.

items.headline: Arrest warrant issued for lawyer Lim Tean after he fails to surrender for a jail term
items.summary: Lim Tean, 61, founder of the People's Voice party, did not surrender at the State Courts on 3 August to begin a sentence of three months and one week under the Legal Profession Act. A warrant was issued and a review set for 17 August after his lawyer and bailor could not reach him.

items.headline: Approved fosterers may keep up to six cats in HDB flats under a new two-year pilot
items.summary: From 3 August, recognised cat fosterers can license and keep up to six cats in HDB flats of three rooms or larger, and up to 10 in private homes, under a scheme consulted on since 2023 and tied to sterilisation requirements.

items.headline: BJP loses the Bankipur by-election in Bihar to Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj
items.summary: Prashant Kishor won the Bankipur assembly seat by more than 19,000 votes over the BJP's Neeraj Kumar, his first electoral contest as Jan Suraaj founder, an upset that sets the tone for the coming Bihar state polls.

items.headline: Government to sell up to 6.5% of LIC as the rupee recovers from a record low
items.summary: New Delhi is offloading up to a 6.5% stake in Life Insurance Corporation at roughly a 10% discount, aiming to raise as much as Rs 314 billion (about US$3.3 billion), as the rupee steadied after foreign investors pulled around US$20 billion from Indian equities.

items.headline: Modi government pushes tax relief for electronics makers and foreign funds
items.summary: An Income-tax amendment moving through the monsoon session would cut taxes for electronics manufacturers and exempt certain foreign institutional investors on specified government-securities earnings, part of a drive to draw manufacturing and portfolio capital.

items.headline: RBI widely expected to hold its key rate at 5.25% at Wednesday's review
items.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee under Governor Sanjay Malhotra is seen keeping the repo rate at 5.25% for a third straight meeting, with 30 of 31 economists in a Bloomberg survey forecasting no change, after retail inflation touched 4.38% in June.

items.headline: Labour overtakes Reform in a poll for the first time in over a year
items.summary: A JL Partners survey put Andy Burnham's Labour on 27% to Nigel Farage's Reform UK on 25%, Labour's first lead in that pollster since March 2025 and its strongest showing since late 2024.

items.headline: Reform UK says it is enlisting tech firms to monitor the south coast for Channel crossings
items.summary: Party official Zia Yusuf said Reform is in talks with technology companies to surveil England's south coast, following its proposal to turn back small boats crossing the Channel.

items.headline: Half of England is in drought after the driest July in nearly 190 years
items.summary: The Environment Agency described an exceptionally serious situation across central, eastern and southern England, where some areas saw as little as 7% of average July rainfall, prompting hosepipe bans affecting millions.

items.headline: Bank of England holds its key rate at 3.75% in a hawkish 6-3 vote
items.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee kept Bank Rate at 3.75% as expected, but three members - Megan Greene, Huw Pill and Catherine Mann - voted for a quarter-point rise, citing upside risks to inflation from energy prices.

items.headline: Italy suspends Schengen free movement with Spain over the Ceuta migrant surge
items.summary: Rome reimposed border checks on non-EU arrivals from Spain for August after tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the enclave of Ceuta from Morocco. It is the first time an EU state has invoked the measure against a country it shares no land border with, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said it undermines EU unity.

items.headline: Japan and the US confirm their first joint yen intervention since 2011
items.summary: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed coordinated dollar-selling to curb volatility, the first joint intervention since 2011, after the dollar neared 163 yen; it fell back to about 157.

items.headline: Cuba suffers its sixth nationwide blackout of 2026 as storms disrupt recovery
items.summary: The national grid collapsed again this week, the island's sixth total blackout of the year, as an electric oscillation and thunderstorms hampered restoration amid chronic fuel shortages and ageing thermal plants.

items.headline: Ferry fire off Indonesia's Madura island kills at least five, with dozens missing
items.summary: The Mutiara Sentosa 2, carrying 271 people from Surabaya to Makassar, caught fire on 2 August off East Java. Rescuers pulled about 225 people to safety, but five bodies were recovered and more than 40 people remained unaccounted for.

items.headline: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic becomes the second-largest outbreak on record
items.summary: The Bundibugyo-strain outbreak centred on Ituri province has passed 3,500 confirmed cases and roughly 1,550 deaths, surpassing the country's 2018-2020 epidemic; there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain.

items.headline: Anthropic signs a $10 billion, six-year cloud-compute deal with startup Volta
items.summary: Anthropic committed $10 billion over six years to the months-old AI-cloud company Volta, which disclosed the same day a $300 million raise and $5 billion in financing at a $2.4 billion valuation, with backing from Nvidia and Michael Dell.

items.headline: Bending Spoons to buy Airtable for $1.28 billion in an all-cash deal
items.summary: The newly public Bending Spoons agreed to acquire the database startup Airtable for about $1.28 billion in cash, its first deal since a July IPO and a steep discount to Airtable's roughly $11 billion 2021 peak.

items.headline: Apple asks a judge to bar OpenAI from using alleged stolen trade secrets
items.summary: Apple escalated its trade-secret suit, telling a federal court that more former employees may have taken confidential hardware data to OpenAI and seeking an injunction to stop its use and force its return.

items.headline: Spotify tops 300 million paying subscribers for the first time
items.summary: Spotify said premium subscribers rose 9% to 300 million in the second quarter, just ahead of forecasts, though its guidance for the current quarter fell short of estimates.

items.headline: Texas orders a halt to new data centers pending grid audits
items.summary: Governor Greg Abbott directed the state utility commission and grid operator ERCOT to audit all new data-center projects, citing the risk that ordinary Texans absorb the cost of the AI-driven build-out.

items.headline: Wall Street hits records as the Dow closes above 54,000 for the first time
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped about 1.7% to finish above 54,000 for the first time, while the S&P 500 rose 1.8% to a record 7,737 and the Nasdaq gained 2.6%, lifted by a tech rebound and easing oil prices.

items.headline: AMD's data-center revenue doubles, but its shares slide on lofty expectations
items.summary: AMD reported second-quarter revenue of $11.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.66 a share, with data-center sales more than doubling to $6.7 billion; the stock still fell more than 7% after hours despite upbeat guidance.

items.headline: SpaceX revenue jumps 92% to $7.81 billion in its first earnings report
items.summary: In its first quarterly report since going public, SpaceX posted revenue of $7.81 billion, up 92%, with a $47.5 billion backlog, though shares fell as much as 8% after hours as capital spending climbed to $18.4 billion.

items.headline: McDonald's sales growth cools as US same-store sales slow to 0.8%
items.summary: McDonald's second-quarter revenue rose 3.7% to $7.10 billion with earnings of $3.32 a share, but US same-store sales grew just 0.8% on softer guest counts; the chain named 26-year veteran Skye Anderson to lead its US business.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's future stays unresolved as F1's summer break rolls on
items.summary: With the grid idle before the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort on 23 August, Max Verstappen has yet to commit to Red Bull amid links to rival teams; German media report Red Bull has offered a longer contract. The team has endured a difficult first season under the sport's new-for-2026 rules.

items.headline: 🏏 Rashid Khan takes a five-wicket haul in the Hundred
items.summary: The Afghanistan spinner claimed five wickets in a men's Hundred match on 2 August, one of the standout bowling displays of the competition's group stage.

items.headline: 🏏 London Spirit are beaten by five wickets in the Hundred women's competition
items.summary: London Spirit's 136 for 7 was chased down with two balls to spare on 4 August, a narrow defeat in the women's Hundred group stage.

items.headline: An experimental HIV vaccine triggers broadly neutralizing antibodies in primates
items.summary: Researchers report in Nature that a germline-targeting protein vaccine elicited broadly neutralizing antibody responses against diverse HIV strains in nonhuman primates, a step toward one of the field's longest-standing barriers.

items.headline: Euclid assembles a census of the earliest known quasars from the cosmic dawn
items.summary: ESA's Euclid mission has identified 31 of the oldest known quasars, more than doubling the count at that epoch, including two seen about 670 million years after the Big Bang shining like a trillion Suns.

fun_fact.headline: The last guillotine execution in France came the same year Star Wars premiered
fun_fact.body: The guillotine was still France's method of execution within living memory. The last person put to death by it, Hamida Djandoubi, was executed on 10 September 1977 - the same year Star Wars first reached cinemas. France kept the guillotine as its official instrument of capital punishment until it abolished the death penalty in 1981.
fun_fact.source: Historical record (Encyclopaedia Britannica; French Ministry of Justice)

puzzle.title: Count the Knights
puzzle.body: On an island where knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie, you meet three islanders - A, B and C. A says: 'Exactly one of us three is a knight.' B says: 'Exactly two of us three are knights.' C says: 'All three of us are knaves.' Who is a knight and who is a knave?
puzzle.approach: Start with the islander whose claim cannot be true if they were a knight, then count.
puzzle.answer: A is a knight; B and C are knaves. C cannot be a knight (the claim 'all three are knaves' would make a knight a liar), so C is a knave and at least one knight exists. If there were two knights, B would be truthful and a knight, forcing A to be a knight too - but then A's 'exactly one knight' claim is false, impossible. So there is exactly one knight: A. B and C both lie. Consistent and unique.

word_puzzle.title: Space Case
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee. Centre letter E; outer letters A L N P S T. Make words of four or more letters, each containing E and using only these seven letters (letters may repeat). Two words are pangrams using all seven.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must contain the centre letter E and use only the seven letters; two words use all seven.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangrams: PLANETS, PLEASANT. Sample words: PLANET, PLANE, PLATE, PLATES, PLEAT, PETAL, PETALS, PASTEL, PANEL, PANELS, PASTE, PANES, LEAPT, SLEPT, SPENT, STEAL, SLATE, STALE, ELATE, STEEP.
